Furnish means to provide or supply something — usually something that is needed, requested, or expected. Think of it as a deliberate, purposeful act of giving, not a casual one. You don't just throw something at someone; you furnish them with what they require.
Meaning 1: To Provide or Supply Something (to Someone)

This is the most common use of "furnish," especially in formal writing and speech. When you furnish something, you supply it — often to someone who needs it or is entitled to it.

The most natural pattern in a sentence is: furnish someone with something, or furnish something to someone.

For example: The lawyer furnished the court with all the necessary documents. Here, the lawyer provided — supplied — documents to the court. You could replace "furnished the court with" with "gave the court" or "provided the court with," and the meaning would be the same. "Furnish" just sounds more deliberate and formal.

More examples:

  • Please furnish us with your contact details. (= Please provide us your contact details.)
  • The company furnished evidence to support its claim.
  • He was unable to furnish a satisfactory explanation.
  • The government was asked to furnish information about the new policy.

Notice something important: "furnish" in this sense is a formal to semi-formal word. In everyday conversation, people tend to say give, provide, or supply. But in legal documents, business correspondence, academic writing, and journalism, "furnish" is very common. If someone writes "Kindly furnish us with your account number," they simply mean "Please give us your account number."
Meaning 2: To Equip a Room or Building with Furniture

This meaning is more physical and specific. To furnish a room or a house means to put furniture and fittings into it — sofas, beds, tables, chairs, wardrobes, desks — so that the space becomes livable, usable, and comfortable.

For example: It took them two months to furnish their new apartment. This means they spent two months buying and placing furniture inside it to make it feel like a proper home.

More examples:

  • The bedroom was furnished with a large bed, a wardrobe, and a study desk.
  • They furnished the office simply — just a desk and two chairs.
  • The hotel suite was beautifully furnished.

This is why in real estate you'll constantly encounter these two terms:

  • A furnished apartment = the apartment already has furniture inside it; you can move in and live comfortably right away.
  • An unfurnished apartment = the apartment has no furniture; you must bring or buy your own.

At first glance, these two meanings seem different — one is about giving information or documents, the other is about placing sofas and beds in a room. But they share the same underlying idea: making something complete by providing what is needed.

When you furnish a room, you complete it — an empty room becomes a functioning, comfortable space. When you furnish someone with evidence or information, you complete their need — they now have what they were missing. In both cases, furnishing means filling a gap with something necessary.

In slightly older or more literary writing, "furnish" can be used even more broadly to mean equip or deck out a space with any kind of fittings or decorations, not just furniture. For example: The hall was furnished with beautiful tapestries and golden candlesticks. The meaning is essentially the same — the hall was equipped, fitted out, made complete — just with decorative items rather than standard furniture.

Furnish = to provide/supply something (especially formally, and especially what is needed), OR to equip a room or building with furniture and fittings. In both uses, the key idea is supplying what is necessary to make something whole, ready, or complete.
